00 · Start here
A growth breakdown for Confetti
Why we made this

You launched Confetti on 28 October with a simple promise: explain your idea, and Confetti takes it from a 3D design to parts at your doorstep. Your launch demo follows one idea all the way to a finished device, and your community page already has desk builds anyone can remix, from a desk companion robot to a Pomodoro timer cube.

3D printing videos already pull millions of plays on TikTok, and "I described it in one sentence and built it" is made for the camera. This board is one idea for showing that every week, from launch week into gift season. It is free, so take whatever is useful.

How to read this board
Use the list on the left, or press P to go frame by frame. On a phone, just scroll.
Creator cards: platform, followers and median views on recent videos.
Please note
Made by hypjam from public information, checked 4 Nov 2026. Nobody at Confetti asked for this, and it is not paid work. The creators named here have not been contacted and have no link to hypjam: they show the kind of people we would cast.
12 maker creators shortlisted, 4 scripts with 32 hooks, and a first month that takes Confetti from launch week into gift season.
Four numbers to remember
28 Oct: your launch on YC and X, with Product Hunt the next day
297K: plays on a maker's video of Claude and ChatGPT designing a 3D printed egg protector (24 Oct)
3.5M: plays on "this is your sign to get a 3D printer", 457 times its account's follower count
27 Nov: Black Friday, the start of the gift season your launch already talks about
Who made this

hypjam is a UGC agency in London. We cast, script, direct and edit creators for consumer startups, and run the best videos as ads.

01 · Why UGC
Why creator videos work
Authenticity
People trust people
"Build hardware with plain English" is a claim. A creator typing one sentence and later holding the finished gadget on camera is proof.
Show, do not tell
The finished thing explains itself
A desk gadget that did not exist until someone described it, sitting on a real desk. Nobody needs the idea explained once they have seen it.
Objections
Answer "I can't do hardware" out loud
A creator who has never opened CAD saying so, then showing the build brief and the parts plan, answers the question before anyone asks it.
A real season
Gift season starts now
Your launch already names personalized gifts for friends. Black Friday is 27 November, and "I made my friend's gift by describing it" is a reason to start this month.
Fuel for ads
Your best ads come from creators
Creator videos that work on TikTok can run as Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads, with 8 openings per script, so the budget follows what people actually watch.
Doesn't feel like an ad
Looks like a normal post
So people actually watch it instead of scrolling past. It is still labelled as an ad, it just does not feel like one.
02 · What we learned
Where Confetti is today
The product
Describe an idea in plain English. Confetti asks questions, proposes a build brief for you to approve, then delivers CAD files (STEP or STL and editable source), a parts plan and build instructions, plus firmware for supported electronics projects. Every revision is saved as a version.
The offer
Start from an idea or remix a public project. Print the files on your own printer, or get printing quotes and order supported printed parts through Confetti, delivered to your door. Publish a design and the community can remix it. In Y Combinator's F26 batch.
Your own channels
Tianyi's launch post on X (28 October) has a 95 second demo that follows one idea to a finished device. The same demo is on YouTube, the launch went up on YC and Product Hunt the same week, and makers can join your Discord.
Already in motion
  • People already use Confetti for a portable analyzer for a physics lab, a custom keyboard, desk companions for the office and gifts for friends (your YC launch).
  • Your community page has desk builds to remix, from a desk companion robot that dozes off when the room goes quiet to a headphone stand with a gamer tag in the base.
  • Your about page: "Sometimes it only has to be something you need."
What that tells us
The idea explains itself in one sentence: say what you want, then hold the real thing. What is missing is volume: makers showing that trip on TikTok and Reels every week.
The timing
You launched on 28 October, just ahead of gift season, and your launch already talks about personalized gifts for friends. Black Friday is 27 November.
Sources: confetti.build (home, how it works, about, explore, support, terms and community design pages), the YC company page and YC launch, Tianyi's posts on X, the YouTube launch demo and Product Hunt, all read 4 Nov 2026.
03 · The category
Maker videos on short video
3D printing and desk builds already pull millions of plays on TikTok: useful prints, desk setups and first printers.
Useful prints
Lists get saved
@engineering_addiction's "19 useful 3d prints you NEED to make!" passed 2.2M plays in September, and a new list goes up several times a week.
Desk setups

AI designs the part

Brands already in the feed

The opening for Confetti
Most maker videos start from a file someone else made. Confetti starts from the viewer's own sentence and ends with the parts on their desk. That is the video we would make every week.
Sources: public TikTok posts by @engineering_addiction, @thehippiehacker, @theworkspacehero, @yungmrm, @kevjeffriesx, @agenomicsphd and @cocoasaesthetic_, read 4 Nov 2026.
04 · The objection
"I've never built hardware": the objection to win
Most viewers will think the same three things: I can't do CAD, I don't own a printer, I've never wired anything. Your pages answer all three, and the answers belong in the videos.
What you already say
  • Describe it in plain English. Confetti asks questions and proposes a build brief you approve.
  • You get CAD files, a parts plan and build instructions, plus firmware for supported electronics.
  • Print it yourself, or order supported printed parts to your door.
  • Or start from a community project and remix it.
How we use it
Every script shows the build brief on screen and ends with the finished thing in hand. Script A is filmed by someone who has never opened CAD, and says so.
Show it as it happens
Creators film Confetti exactly as it behaves on the day, on their own account, with the parts they really printed or ordered. Nothing is mocked up.
Safe desk builds
Desk projects only: USB powered or no electronics at all. Never mains power, no weapons, and care with batteries, heat and moving parts, as your terms ask.
What creators never say
No "anyone can build anything" or "zero skills needed", no delivery dates, and nothing your pages do not say Confetti does.
Sources: confetti.build how it works, support and terms (updated 27 Oct 2026), and the YC launch, read 4 Nov 2026.
05 · Audience
Who to sell to first
Start here
Desk setup fans with a printer
They already print things for their desk. A design they described themselves is the next step up from someone else's file. Formats A and B.
Start here
People with an idea and no CAD
"Something for your desk, your kitchen, your garden" is your own line. These viewers have the idea and never had the tools. Format A.
Broadest reach
Gift-givers
Your launch already names personalized gifts for friends. In late November that is everyone looking for something a store does not sell. Format D.
Early adopters
Builders who vibe code
"AI has changed who can build software. We believe hardware is next." Claude and ChatGPT fans who want to make something they can hold. Format C.
Where we would start
Desk setup fans with a printer first: the step from video to building is short, and their builds look great on camera. Gift-givers follow from late November. Every creator we cast and every audience we target is an adult.
06 · The moment
From launch week into gift season
You launched on 28 October. The next eight weeks run straight into the season when people want to make and give something nobody else has.
Now to 15 November
Desk builds from one sentence (Script A) and community remixes (Script B) are planned and filmed. Each creator builds what they show.
16 November to Black Friday
First videos go live, and comment-picked builds (Script C) start a weekly series. Gift builds (Script D) are filmed and posted before 27 November.
December
Gift videos lead. The hooks and creators that drive sign-ups move into TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads.
What this needs from you
  • Accounts for each creator with room for a few builds and revisions
  • The builds and parts you would most like shown, so creators stick to supported projects
  • A sign-up link or code per creator, so sign-ups trace back to videos
Why start now
Launch week gave Confetti a demo that explains itself. Creator videos started now are tested and cut by the time gift shopping peaks.
07 · The first month
Your first four weeks
Week 1 · 9-15 Nov
You approve the shortlist and the 4 formats. We sign creators and send each a script with 8 hooks. Each creator plans their first desk build in Confetti.
Week 2 · 16-22 Nov
First videos come in, and we review each within 48 hours. Desk builds and remixes go live first, and the first hook tests start.
Week 3 · 23-29 Nov
Gift week: Script D goes live before Black Friday on 27 November, and budget moves to the hooks and creators that drive sign-ups.
Week 4 · 30 Nov-6 Dec
Results review together: sign-ups by creator and by ad, and the plan for December gift builds.
If it is a yes this week
Agreement signed and creators planning their first builds by Friday. First videos live within 14 days of the scripts being signed off.

Takeaway
Useful, simple builds break out from small accounts, and the AI design angle already pulls hundreds of thousands of plays. So we would run your launch demo and creator volume side by side, testing 8 hooks per script.
Where the market is
Printer brands like Bambu Lab and Creality pay makers for print videos, and OpenAI has paid a creator to show ChatGPT helping design a 3D print. Tianyi calls Confetti "the first AI platform for vibe-manufacturing", and its videos can show the whole trip, from one sentence to the parts on a desk.
10 · Script A
Script A: One sentence to my desk
The brief

Where: TikTok and Instagram Reels on the creator's account, YouTube Shorts, then TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads to confetti.build (15s and 30s cuts)

Length: 40-45s master. 30s cut: shots 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9. 15s cut: shots 1, 2, 3 and 9 (finished gadget, disclosure, the sentence, the call to action).

Goal: Sign-ups at confetti.build

Who films it: A US desk-setup or 3D printing creator, 18+, who has never used CAD (said on camera only if true). Builds a desk gadget with no electronics, or USB powered and solderless, printed on their own printer or ordered through Confetti where the project supports it. Filmed at their own desk on a phone, with a screen recording of Confetti on the day.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)
  1. I've never opened CAD. I typed one sentence.I have never opened CAD in my life. I typed one sentence, and now this is on my desk.
  2. This [headphone stand] started as one sentenceThis [headphone stand] started as one sentence I typed.
  3. I didn't design this. I described it.I didn't design this. I described it.
  4. POV: you describe a desk gadget, then you're holding itDescribe a desk gadget, then hold it. That's the whole video.
  5. Things on my desk I made without knowing CAD, part 1Things on my desk I made without knowing any CAD. Part one.
  6. What I typed vs what I'm holdingHere's what I typed, and here's what I'm holding.
  7. No CAD. No modeling. One sentence.No CAD, no modeling. One sentence.
  8. My desk needed a [cable hook]. So I described one.My desk needed a [cable hook], so I just described one.

Rules for this video

FTC: 'Ad | Paid partnership with Confetti' on screen from 0s to the end, a spoken disclosure by 0:05, the platform's paid-partnership label switched on (TikTok content disclosure, Instagram 'Paid partnership', YouTube 'Includes paid promotion'), and the caption opens with the disclosure. The paid cuts run as Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads from the creator's handle. Desk-safe build only: no electronics, or USB powered and solderless; never mains power, no loose batteries, no weapons. The creator follows Confetti's build instructions and each part's ratings, and finishes the build before filming the final shots. Confetti is shown exactly as it behaves on the day: never mock up a brief, a design or a file, and name only what this project delivered. Supported parts and projects only. If parts were ordered, show the real order, and say nothing about delivery times, prices or plans. 'Never used CAD' only if true. No absolutes such as 'anyone can build anything' or 'zero skills'. Blur names, emails and addresses on screen.

Why it should convert
It shows the whole promise in one video, from a sentence to a brief, a design, the files and the finished gadget. The first-timer angle answers 'I can't do hardware' before anyone asks, and opening on the finished thing gives a hook that survives a 15 second cut.

13 · Script D
Script D: I made my friend's gift by describing it
The brief

Where: TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts on the creator's account; the best cuts run as Meta partnership ads and TikTok Spark Ads from 16 November to Black Friday and through December

Length: 40-50s master. 20s cut: shots 1, 2, 3, 7 and 8.

Goal: Sign-ups at confetti.build

Who films it: A US or UK 3D printing or desk-setup creator, 18+, making a real gift for an adult friend who agrees on camera to appear. The gift is a desk piece, such as a headphone stand with the friend's gamer tag in the base, printed at home or ordered through Confetti where the project supports it.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)
  1. I made my friend's gift by describing itI made my friend's gift just by describing it.
  2. Not from a store. From a sentence.This gift isn't from a store. It's from a sentence.
  3. For the friend who has everything: something that didn't existFor the friend who has everything, I made something that didn't exist.
  4. POV: their gamer tag is built into the giftTheir gamer tag is literally built into this gift.
  5. I typed what [Sam] loves into one sentenceI typed everything [Sam] loves into one sentence.
  6. Their reaction to a gift nobody else hasWatch [Sam]'s face when they open a gift nobody else has.
  7. Gift idea: describe it, print it, wrap itGift idea for this year: describe it, print it, wrap it.
  8. The most personal gift I've ever madeThis is the most personal gift I've ever made. [Only if true.]
Shot list
TimeWhat we seeOn screenSpoken
0-2sA wrapped gift on the desk next to the laptop open on Confetti.[Hook] + 'Ad | Paid partnership with Confetti' label for the whole video[Hook spoken line]
2-5sCreator to camera.Ad | Paid partnership with ConfettiConfetti paid me to make this video, so it's an ad. The gift is real.
5-11sScreen recording: typing the gift sentence into Confetti.'[a headphone stand for Sam's [headphones], with [their gamer tag] in the base and a cable hook]'I described it in one go: what it's for, what it has to fit, and their gamer tag in the base.
11-17sScreen recording: the build brief, then one change saved as a new version.build brief | '[make the trim orange]' | version [2]It showed me a build brief, I asked for [orange trim], and that's version two.
17-24sPrinting at home as a timelapse, or printed parts arriving if ordered through Confetti. Only the version that really happened.[printed at home] or [ordered through Confetti][Home version: Then I printed it.] [Order version, only if true: I ordered the printed parts through Confetti.]
24-30sFinishing and wrapping.wrapping it up[One line, your words.]
30-40sThe friend, an adult who agreed on camera, unwraps it at their own desk. Their real reaction, uncut.[their real first words][Their real reaction.]
40-48sCreator to camera with the gift in place on the friend's desk.confetti.build | describe the giftIt's called Confetti. Describe the gift at confetti.build and make something nobody else has.
Product moment and call to action

Confetti on screen at 0:00 beside the wrapped gift, named in the disclosure by 0:05. Hero moment 0:05-0:17: the friend's details go into one sentence and come back as a build brief and a design. The unwrapping at 0:30 is the payoff the 20s cut keeps.

CTA: Describe a gift at confetti.build. Paid cuts go to confetti.build through the creator's link, from 16 November to Black Friday and through December.

Caption
Ad | Paid partnership with @[Confetti's handle on this platform]. Made [Sam]'s gift by describing it: [the gift, one line]. confetti.build #ad #confetti #giftideas #3dprinting #desksetup
Rules for this video

FTC: 'Ad | Paid partnership with Confetti' on screen from 0s to the end, a spoken disclosure by 0:05, the platform's paid-partnership label switched on (TikTok content disclosure, Instagram 'Paid partnership', YouTube 'Includes paid promotion'), and the caption opens with the disclosure. The friend is an adult who agrees on camera before filming and sees the video before it posts; no children on camera; no names, emails or addresses on screen beyond a first name or gamer tag they approve. Desk-safe gift only: no electronics, or USB powered and solderless; no mains power. Shown exactly as it happened: never mock up a design or an order. No delivery dates, prices or 'in time for' promises. 'Most personal gift' only if true.

Why it should convert
Gift videos ride a season people already spend in, and the unwrapping gives viewers a reason to watch to the end. Personalisation is the one thing a store cannot do, and Confetti's own launch already names gifts for friends.

16 · Ads
How the paid ads would run
1 · Film
Each script is shot once, with 8 different openings.
→
2 · Launch
Each opening runs as its own ad, from the creator's handle as a partnership ad.
→
3 · Read
After a few days we compare cost per sign-up and how many people watch past 3 seconds.
4 · Cut
The weakest openings switch off and the budget moves to the best two.
→
5 · Remix
Winning hooks get new bodies and new creators.
→
6 · Refresh
New creator videos every week, so the ads never go stale.
Where the ads point
confetti.build, through one link per creator, so every sign-up traces back to the video that drove it. The same videos run as TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads, shown to adults interested in 3D printing, desk setups and electronics.
Why partnership ads
Ads that run from a creator's own handle look like that creator's post, not a brand ad. That is the format these videos are built for.
What we would need
Access to your TikTok and Meta ad accounts (or we run them from ours), sign-ups by link, and a weekly look at the numbers.
17 · Process
How a campaign runs, step by step
1 · Brief
You tell us the goal, the audience and what can and can't be said about Confetti.
→
2 · Cast
We shortlist creators by niche, location and median views. You pick.
→
3 · Offer
We send each creator the brief, the dates and the rate.
4 · Sign
A written agreement with every creator, covering usage and disclosure.
→
5 · Scripts
One per format: 8 hooks, a shot list, screens to record and a caption.
→
6 · Film and upload
Creators film on their phones and upload to a private folder only we see.
7 · Review
We check every video within 48 hours. Nothing posts unapproved.
→
8 · Post
On the creator's own account, with the ad disclosure and the paid-partnership label.
→
9 · Pay and report
Creators paid within 7 days of going live. You get a report every Monday.
Where creators talk to us
One hypjam Discord for every creator. Each campaign gets a private channel group for chat, scripts and posted links that only its creators and your team can see.
Builds
Each signed creator plans their build in Confetti on their own account, prints it at home or orders the printed parts where the project supports it, and assembles it before filming the finish. What shows on screen is really theirs.
18 · Reporting
What we report, and when
Every video
Views, how many people stay past 3 seconds, average watch time, saves, shares and comments.
Every creator link
A tracking link for each creator, so sign-ups trace back to the video that drove them.
Every Monday
A short report: every video, the hooks that won, sign-ups by creator, and what we change next.
Every month
A review call: spend, sign-ups, cost per result on anything run as an ad, and the plan for next month.
19 · Rules
Rules we never break
Disclosure
"Ad | Paid partnership with Confetti" on screen, said in the first seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. That is what the FTC asks for.
Who films
Adults only (18+). Creators use Confetti themselves before they talk about it.
What gets said
Nothing your own pages do not say Confetti does. No invented numbers. We never pay for a positive opinion, only for the video.
Safe desk builds
Desk projects only, USB powered or no electronics. Never mains power, no weapons, and care with batteries, heat, moving parts and sharp edges, as your terms ask. Creators follow the build instructions and each part's own ratings.
Credit and licences
Community designs are shown only with their maker's OK or when they are Confetti's own, credited by handle and used under their licence. Only supported parts and projects appear on camera.
How we run it
Every video reviewed within 48 hours before it posts. Creators paid within 7 days of going live.
